elements.text: UniverseGate lets you build a network of energy-powered portals, travel between villages and reach a mysterious dimension: the Rift.
Chapters follow the mod's progression. Animated scenes show each build block by block: ◀ and ▶▶ change step, || pauses, ↻ turns the scene. Hover an item to see its name.
The UniverseGate advancement tab also follows the whole adventure.

1. Produce energy (Energy chapter).
2. Build your first portal.
3. Force an unstable link to the Rift during a thunderstorm.
4. Bring back from the Rift what you need to craft a real Portal Controller.
Long before us, this world was home to a technologically advanced race: the Builders. They covered the world with portals, even in villages. Then they vanished. Nobody knows why… not yet.
One day, one of their portals opened a breach between universes. None of it was planned: the breach set off a cosmic explosion, like a small big bang, that gave birth to a new dimension.
The Rift was born by accident, like a bug in the fabric of the world. Everything there is black and white, the ground floats in the void, and a strange energy flows everywhere.
The breach never truly closed. When lightning overloads a Portal Core, its address gets scrambled and the portal slips through the breach: it opens onto the Rift, unstable.

The first Builders to cross the breach got stuck in the Rift. So that it would never happen again, they added safety protocols to every Portal Core: in the Rift, a portal draws on the dimension's natural energy to power itself, so the way back always stays open.
Rift Shades and Rift Beasts are errors: beings torn from several universes and dragged into this dimension by the breach.
The Rift Cubes, those huge white temples, remain a mystery. Even the Builders did not know who built them, or what their guardians protect.

The Builders also set up portals in villages. Over time, villagers lost the know-how. You are the one who teaches them again: Portal Engineers are grateful, and they show it when you meet their expeditions.
Everything runs on energy, measured in FE. A network starts with an Energy Condenser: both the battery (20,000 FE) and the heart of the network.

captions: Place Solar Panels. They must see the sky and only work during the day.
Connect them with Energy Conduits.
The Energy Condenser stores what they produce.
The Energy Monitor shows stored energy, capacity and connected devices.
At night, a Combustion Generator burns any furnace fuel, or Rift Crystals (24,000 FE each), up to 480 FE/s.

elements.text: UniverseGate energy speaks NeoForge FE and, on Fabric, Team Reborn Energy (1 FE = 1 E). Cables from Stellaris and other mods plug into condensers and conduits (in and out), up to 1,000 FE per tick per block. None of these mods is required.
A portal is built around a Portal Core: 6 Portal Ring Segments, or a classic 5×6 frame (3×4 inside) with the core at the bottom centre. Both methods can be mixed.

captions: Place the Portal Core: it is the bottom centre of the ring.
Hold a Portal Ring Segment near the core: a translucent preview shows where it goes. Right-click to place it.
Keep building the ring, segment by segment.
The last segment closes the ring.
The complete ring assembles itself: the portal is ready.
Connect the core to an energy network with conduits. Opening costs at least 1,200 FE (more with distance and across dimensions), then 120 FE/s.
Place a Portal Controller. Clip a Crocodile Clip on the controller and one on the portal, then join them with Electric Wire.
Dial another portal of the network: it opens.

elements.text: Name your portal, then pick a destination in the controller. The controller needs Rift materials (Void Block, Light Beam Emitter): for your first trip, force an unstable link (The Rift chapter).
The Mobile Portal Controller dials from your hand near a portal. The Portal Redstone Activator opens a preset destination on each pulse.

Large villages (at least 9 adult villagers) get their own gate, with a Natural Portal Controller that opens for free. The Portal Engineer, a new profession, sometimes travels the network and rewards players who are there when they arrive.
Your first trip to the Rift is powered by lightning.

captions: You need a complete portal.
Craft a Lightning Antenna (4 blocks tall) and place it out in the open.
Wire the antenna's base to the portal: Crocodile Clips on the portal, then red and blue Electric Wire.
Wait for a thunderstorm, or make one with the weather machine.
Lightning strikes the antenna: the charge runs down the wires and opens an unstable link to the Rift. Careful, it is unstable!

elements.text: The Rift is a dark, void-based dimension. Find Kelo Wood, Rift Meat and Rift Crystals there: from Rift Shades, or as clusters on the ground (pickaxe, Fortune works).
Rift Cubes are huge white temples. Their Guardian, a giant Rift Shade, wakes up the first time someone nears the emitter: it drops a Rift Core.
Portals in the Rift run on ambient energy: the way back is easy if you have a frame.

captions: Place the Meteorological Controller.
Next to it (within 1 block), stack 2 Meteorological Condensers.
On top, place the Meteorological Catalyst.
Put an Energy Crystal in it: each activation uses it up.
Connect the tower to the energy network.
Add a Parabola on the same network (120 FE/s). After a 5 minute charge, pick Clear, Rain or Thunder (2,500 FE, 10 minutes).

elements.text: Thunder is the easiest way to strike your antenna.
This part of the mod is still in development. It will be covered here later.
Aim at a mob (up to 14 blocks away) with the DNA Extractor and hold right-click for 20 seconds. Each extraction costs 64 Rift Crystals. A sample has 100 uses, plus 50 per level of Unbreaking.

captions: You need a running Dark Energy Generator.
Link it to the Mob Cloner with Dark Energy Conduits.
The cloner needs free space above it.
Put the cloner and its controller on the same energy network, insert the DNA and start cloning.

elements.text: A clone costs at least 1 billion FE, more for monsters and bosses: a ZPC is practically required.
The live view shows the destination through an open portal. Turn it off if your PC struggles or with some shaders.
